policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'when he heard those words' renders a temporal infinitive construct; both the qere kaph (כְּשָׁמְעוֹ, 'as/when he heard') and the ketiv beth (בשמעו, 'in his hearing' = 'when he heard') yield the same English 'when he heard'. No italics or textual note; the base qere fallback carries the projection.

ASV 'by the time the sun is hot' renders a temporal infinitive construct; the qere kaph (כְּחֹם, 'as the sun is hot') and the ketiv beth (בחם, 'in the heat of') are both compatible with this English, and 'by the time' does not favour either preposition. No italics or textual note; the base qere fallback carries the projection.
